brief: An island-town cottage lot: Pelton House, a 19th-century Lake Erie house; see the photo for its massing, porch and trim. One photo; year estimated. Older than 1970: the Lake Erie shore towns that stand in for Victory Bay's island streets (Vermilion, Sandusky, Put-in-Bay) were built 1840-1920, and Commons has almost no newer cottages there. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Pelton House (Vermilion): a white Greek Revival upright with long one-storey wings and black shutters, extended with a porte-cochere on the left and a later wing on the right; signs, a monument sign and a parking drive -- a house converted to a funeral home or office on the main road

why.note: big houses on the main road become funeral homes and offices; the porte-cochere marks a funeral home
